forecasts.reason: Tip is really 10 epochs, so going to 8.5 cuts about 15% of steps; at about 0.6 pp per epoch that costs about 0.9 pp and drops below 0.756 (likely below 0.753). Time scales nearly linearly.
Lookahead/EMA already averages the noisy tail and Muon keeps weight norm fixed, so the 0.07 to 0 change in the floor is mostly redundant: about +0.1 pp, under the 0.3 pp bar. Time is unchanged.

Pixel fraction 0.755 to 0.639 gives about 12% time cut, but 20 px loses more than linearly (E007 lost 0.59 pp for 24%). Likely lands at or below the bar, so the time-per-pp trade is about neutral compared with cutting epochs.
The last group is about 37% of conv FLOPs, and 576 to 512 saves about 5.6% overall, so about 3-5% time. CIFAR-100 is width-sensitive at 100 classes, so about -0.3 pp. Both bars are borderline.
Recipe unchanged, so the seeds 0-2 result reproduces. Held-out mean is likely within 0.3 pp with per-seed std of about 0.2-0.35 pp.

Batch 2000 at about 28 ms/step is mostly GPU-bound, so graphs save only launch overhead (about 2-6%). Capturing the optimizer and the per-step LR plus fused-SGD float lr is a bug and leak risk (fat right tail).
BN buffers are already lookahead-averaged and last stats came from 32 px batches, so the gain is about 0.1-0.2 pp. A new forward shape in timed code risks cuDNN autotune cost beyond 0.15 s.

cruxes: Is the tip really 10 epochs (HYP) while the ideas say 9? This decides whether I009's '8.5' is a 0.5- or a 1.5-epoch cut, and whether it is feasible.
What is the accuracy-per-epoch slope with Muon+EMA+resizing on? If it is at or below 0.4 pp/epoch, cutting epochs beats every other lever; at 0.7 or more, the 0.6 pp margin buys only about 0.5 s.
How much of the 28 ms/step is CPU/launch overhead under the 4-CPU pin compared with GPU compute at batch 2000? This sets the ceiling for CUDA graphs (I014) and for resizing's time-to-pixel linearity.

W3 (cost lens), after E007. Code truth: HYP epochs=10, batch 2000 (25 steps/epoch, 250 steps). The idea texts call this '9 epochs'.

Measured ledger (compiled):
- E004: SGD, 9.04 s, 0.7486.
- E005: +EMA, +0.06 s for +0.97 pp.
- E006: +Muon/bs2000, +0.35 s for +0.66 pp (0.7649).
- E007: +resizing, −2.1 s (−22%) for −0.59 pp (0.7590). Time tracks pixel count nearly linearly, which suggests the GPU is the bottleneck, not launches.

Exchange rates:
- Epochs: about 0.7 s per epoch, about 0.5-0.7 pp per epoch, so about 1.2 s/pp.
- Resizing: about 3.6 s/pp so far, with worse rates expected at 20 px.
- Margin: 0.6 pp over 0.753, about 0.3 pp over a safe 0.756, so about 0.5 epoch (about 0.35 s) can be spent.

Remaining free levers: CUDA graphs (small, risky); width 512 (about 4% time, about 0.3 pp, neutral); LR to 0 and BN recompute (both small, under 0.2 pp, given EMA).

Best plan: spend the margin on epochs (about 9.5), then look for cheap accuracy (LS/wd/lr retune) to buy more epoch cuts.
